category_title: Gifted Hispanic female underachieving due to perceived inadequacy and lack of task relevance
minimal_context: The student and tutor are working one-on-one in English class to prepare for the FCAT reading assessment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's work on preparing for the FCAT reading assessment. Please read this passage and answer the questions.

STUDENT: I'm just going to use test-taking strategies to defeat this assessment instead of actually reading it.

TUTOR: Why don't you try using the insight and divergent thinking you use in your writing assignments?

STUDENT: I don't think of that as a strategy for this. The FCAT is just about analysis and test-taking strategies, not finesse.

TUTOR: Just do your best on the reading assessment.

STUDENT: I'm just going to stop trying so hard. Failing this makes me feel like an 'inadequate student' and failure is inevitable anyway. I don't want to define myself as the 'intellectual type'.

options.A: Require three revisions per writing assignment and only grade the final draft during one-on-one sessions.
options.B: Provide easy, independent reading assignments selected by the tutor that the student can complete unassisted with 80% accuracy.
options.C: Engage in shared discourse and direct instruction in coping strategies during one-on-one conversations about the assessment.
options.D: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level FCAT reading questions based on the student's reading level.
